body.statement: If \(0<\kappa\le-\log(1-\alpha)/\overline m_*\), then \(D_{\mathrm{det}}(\kappa)=L\exp(-\kappa m_*)\). At each fixed \(s\), the conditional value is \(L\exp\{-\kappa m(s)\}\). Every fixed-share optimizer reports \(\Theta\) at the zero table and a singleton at every nonzero table. A globally optimal observed-share policy is characterized exactly by \(C(s,0)=\Theta\) and \(\sum_{x\ne0}P_{\eta,\kappa}(x)\ell(C(s,x))\le L\exp(-\kappa m_*)-L\exp\{-\kappa M(\eta)\}\) for every \(\eta\). The share \(s^*\) is the unique minimizer of \(m(s)\), the associated lower-endpoint nuisance is least favorable for every optimizer, and additional least-favorable configurations occur exactly when the displayed allowance binds.
body.justification: The theorem gives an exact minimax value and a complete optimizer description in the sparse phase where regular PPML intervals fail most severely.
body.gap: Evans, Hansen, and Stark (2005) provide duality but no multivariate-Poisson value or optimizer characterization; Kabaila and Byrne (2001) treat one scalar Poisson mean.
body.consumer: Researchers with rare cohort-time outcomes can report the shortest uniformly honest deterministic connected interval policy and know precisely when nonzero tables permit extra length.
